newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Banco de Colombia holder meeting delayed.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Colombia holder meeting delayed.

text.p: An annual meeting of Banco de Colombia shareholders was suspended Friday after the family-owned bank's leading stockholders failed to put in an appearance.

"It was the Gilinskis' intention to attend the meeting to give shareholders good news about the negotiation you all know about, but problems with flight connections prevented them doing so," Luis Fernando Gaviria, a member of the bank's board of directors, told the meeting.

Gaviria later told Reuters that members of the Gilinski family, who bought Banco de Colombia in 1994, were still in Europe negotiating the sale of a stake in the bank to Spain's Banco Central Hispano.
Gaviria said he was unable to comment on the negotiations and Banco de Colombia's executive president, Federico Rengifo, also declined comment.
The shareholders' meeting will be rescheduled for some time after April 11, bank officials said.

A preliminary accord reached between Banco de Colombia and Banco Central Hispano last year called for the sale of anywhere between 25 and 36 percent of the bank -- Colombia's second largest in terms of assets -- to BCH.
